drivingQuestion: Does 'everyone substitutes' mean substitution is permitted ab initio?
outcomeNote: Rav Yehuda rereads the mishna so both clauses concern effect, not permission

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא: אָמְרַתְּ ״הַכֹּל מְמִירִין״ — לְכַתְּחִילָּה, וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי ״לֹא שֶׁאָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהָמִיר אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם הֵמִיר מוּמָר״ — דִּיעֲבַד!
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara «notes» an apparent contradiction in the mishna: «This» mishna «itself» is «difficult: You say» that «everyone substitutes» a non-sacred animal for a consecrated one, which indicates that substitution may be performed «ab initio. And then you teach:» That is «not» to say «that it is permitted for a person to effect substitution; rather,» it means only «that if one» unlawfully «substituted» a non-sacred animal for a consecrated animal, «the substitution takes effect,» indicating that it is effective only «after the fact.»

segments.he: וְתִיסְבְּרָא ״הַכֹּל מְמִירִין״ — לְכַתְּחִילָּה? אַדְּקַשְׁיָא לָךְ מִמַּתְנִיתִין, תִּיקְשֵׁי לָךְ קְרָא! דִּכְתִיב ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ״.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «And can you understand» the phrase: «Everyone substitutes,» as indicating that substitution may be performed «ab initio?» If so, «before the mishna poses a difficulty for you, the verse should pose a difficulty for you, as it is written: “He shall not alter it, nor substitute it”» (Leviticus 27:10). The verse clearly states that it is prohibited to perform substitution.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הָכִי קָתָנֵי — הַכֹּל מַתְפִּיסִין בִּתְמוּרָה, אֶחָד אֲנָשִׁים וְאֶחָד נָשִׁים, לֹא שֶׁאָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהָמִיר, שֶׁאִם הֵמִיר — מוּמָר, וְסוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav Yehuda says: This» is what the mishna «is teaching: Everyone can apply» the status of a consecrated animal to a non-sacred animal «by» the act of «substitution, both men and women.» But that is «not» to say «that it is permitted for a person to effect substitution, as, if» one «did effect substitution,» the «substitution takes effect» only after the fact, «and he incurs the forty» lashes.

moves.summary: the opening and closing clauses of the mishna conflict (ab initio vs after the fact)
moves.about: the mishna's 'everyone substitutes' implies ab initio permission, while 'not that a person is permitted' implies only after the fact

moves.summary: the premise that 'everyone substitutes' means ab initio is untenable given the verse
moves.about: whether 'everyone substitutes' can mean ab initio at all, given the verse forbids substitution

moves.summary: the mishna teaches that substitution takes effect for all, men and women, and the substituter is flogged
moves.about: resolves the internal contradiction in the mishna
